Add primary `bridge`-noun spellings for the three surviving bridge verbs, migrate every
enumerated in-tree consumer, and preserve the old spellings as compatibility entrypoints for
workflows and environments that have not migrated yet:

* `rebar bridge-fsck`   -> `rebar bridge fsck`
* `rebar bridge-probe`  -> `rebar bridge check-access`
* `rebar jira-onboard`  -> `rebar bridge setup`

Carved out of `4752-3afb-e8bd-448a`, which now owns only the `bridge` verb-group registration.
`depends_on 4752` because the noun and its dispatch must exist before verbs can attach to it.

## These are RENAMES, not new features — this is what the reviews caught

`check-access` is NOT new work. `bridge-probe` already ships the identical create/label/search/
delete Jira round-trip (`src/rebar/_engine/jira-capability-probe.py`, launched via
`_cli/__init__.py:163`'s `_bridge_probe`), so this is a rename plus consumer migration, not an
implementation. `bridge setup` is likewise the EXISTING `jira-onboard` wizard renamed
(`src/rebar/_cli/_jira_onboard.py`), which already implements persist-config-then-probe. Scoping
these as renames is the whole point of the split: the work is enumerating and migrating consumers,
and each rename's consumer set is listed below rather than left implicit.

## Why `check-access` stays its own verb rather than becoming a flag (carried from `4752`)

All three narrowing-flag precedents — `flux check --pre`, `dbt debug --connection`,
`gh auth status` — are READ-ONLY, and none mutates the remote. The precedent therefore does not
transfer to an operation that CREATES AND DELETES A REAL JIRA ISSUE. `fsck` audits your records;
`check-access` proves your access. They are different questions with different blast radii.

`setup` calls `check-access` as its final validation step (this is already how `jira-onboard`
ends, via `_jira_onboard.py:196-200` invoking `_bridge_probe` with the just-persisted settings
injected as an env overlay; the rename must preserve that overlay behaviour and the
`--no-validate` escape hatch).
